builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
summary: The study replaces manual, expert-designed LLM compression pipelines (quantization, format conversion, inference code) with a terminal-based coding agent that autonomously searches compression strategies under a storage and time budget. Adopting this approach costs agent compute and wall-clock time for iterative experiments, plus a 3.4% perplexity increase and roughly a 2.2-point downstream accuracy drop relative to BF16. Failures include misleading local likelihood rankings (17 of 79 reversed by complete-model feedback) and generation or inference defects that perplexity verification alone does not detect.
rationale: This is a benchmark of agent capability rather than a deployable compression method, so the reader should track it while continuing to use established quantization tooling directly.
technique: Coding agents performing autonomous LLM compression

claims.statement: The study replaces manual, expert-designed LLM compression pipelines (quantization, format conversion, inference code) with a terminal-based coding agent that autonomously searches compression strategies under a storage and time budget. Adopting this approach costs agent compute and wall-clock time for iterative experiments, plus a 3.4% perplexity increase and roughly a 2.2-point downstream accuracy drop relative to BF16. Failures include misleading local likelihood rankings (17 of 79 reversed by complete-model feedback) and generation or inference defects that perplexity verification alone does not detect.
Best agent designs achieve an average 3.4% perplexity increase over BF16 and 77.33% downstream accuracy versus 79.56% for BF16; 29 of 36 submissions pass verification
